name: Glenashen
blurb: One of the quieter Antrim glens: a sheep-walled hill, a ruined cottage, a river in a hurry and a sporting lease the Trust would very much like back. Nobody has walked it in a generation.

lines: Sheep-bitten grass, bracken on the slopes, and not a hare in sight.
The sheep gone, the fences down, and the first rowan up in the gully.
Heather and gorse, ferns on the river bank, a hare in the open field.
Wild glen, birch and hazel in the gullies, and a hare in every field.

ranger: Sheep-bitten grass and bracken. A glen with the life taken out of it, and not a hare in sight.
The sheep are gone, the fences are down, and there's a rowan up in the gully.
Heather and gorse, ferns on the river bank. I saw a hare in the open field yesterday.
A wild glen, birch and hazel in the gully, and every bird in Antrim, it seems.
